problem:
Find the second-degree Taylor polynomial ${P}_{2}(x)$ of $f(x)={e}^{2x}$ about $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡3.$

${P}_{2}(x)=$
{{field-1}}$\,+$
{{field-2}}$(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)\,+$
{{field-3}}${(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}^{2}$
worked_solution:
To find the second-degree Taylor polynomial about $x=\operatorname{ln}⁡3,$ we plug $a=\operatorname{ln}⁡3$ into the general formula to give

$$
{P}_{2}(x)=f(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)+{f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3){(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}^{2}.
$$

So, we need to work out $f(\operatorname{ln}⁡3),$ ${f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3),$ and ${f}^{″}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ={e}^{2x} & ⟹ &  & f(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =9 \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =2{e}^{2x} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =18 \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =4{e}^{2x} & ⟹ &  & {f}^{″}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3) & =36\end{aligned}
$$

We now plug the results for $f(\operatorname{ln}⁡3),$ ${f}^{′}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3),$ and ${f}^{″}(\operatorname{ln}⁡3)$ into our second-degree Taylor polynomial. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =9+18(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)+36\cdot \frac{1}{2}{(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}^{2} \\  & =9+18(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)+18{(x-\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
